A seat is one person's access to one vendor's account on AEC Integrations. Seats have no price and no limit on how many your company holds. What a seat can change depends partly on each product's plan, Free or Managed, set out below.

A field that AEC Integrations corrected and locked shows "Set by AEC Integrations" with the reason, and no seat can change it until AEC Integrations lifts the lock. [Owning an integration](/docs/vendors/owning-an-integration) explains how a lock works.

## Sign in

Go to the [sign-in page](/auth/login) and choose **Continue with Google**, or enter your email and choose **Email me a sign-in link**. Use the address your seat was granted to. There is no password.

Once you are signed in, the vendor portal opens on your company's overview. Its tabs are **Vendor Overview**, **Profile**, **Products**, **Messages**, **Changes** and **Seats**, plus **Billing** for owners. Each product has its own tabs, including **Integrations**. [Your dashboard](/docs/vendors/your-dashboard) walks through them.

One account holds a seat on one vendor. If you need seats at two companies, use a separate email address for each.

## How seats are granted

There are three ways to get a seat:

- **An approved claim.** The person who claimed the listing becomes an owner of the account. See [Claiming your vendor listing](/docs/vendors/claiming-your-listing).
- **An invitation from a colleague.** The person invited becomes a member.
- **AEC Integrations adds one** at your company's request. That seat is an owner.

Owners and members can do the same things with your company's listings. The difference is that only owners manage seats, see the **Billing** tab, add a product, and accept or decline a proposed one. See [Billing](/docs/vendors/billing).

## Invite a colleague

Owners invite from the **Seats** tab. Choose **Invite**, enter your colleague's email address, and choose **Send invite**. Any address works. Your colleague must sign in with the address you invited.

- An invitation expires after 14 days.
- **Resend** sends it again. You can send each invitation up to four times, a few minutes apart.
- **Revoke** cancels an invitation that has not been accepted.
- Your company can send up to 10 invitations a day.

Invited colleagues join as members. Members cannot invite others.

If your colleague's account already holds a seat at another company, the invite page says the account can't join your team. They need to sign in with a different address, and you need to invite that address.

## Remove a colleague

Owners remove a seat with **Remove** on the **Seats** tab. The person loses access to the vendor portal straight away. Their account stays, as an ordinary account that can still write reviews.

You cannot remove your own seat from the portal. If you are leaving your company, ask an owner to remove you. If you are the last owner, contact us first so the account is not left without one.

If the last seat on your company's account goes, your listing stays yours. Nobody can edit it until your company has a seat again, and we do not overwrite it in the meantime. Your claimed integrations stay claimed. Open questions about your integrations come to us until a seat returns, then go back to you.

## Your account and your seat

Your seat belongs to your account on AEC Integrations, the one you sign in with.

- Colleagues with a seat on your vendor account see your display name in the vendor portal. You set it on your [account page](/account). See [Your account and your data](/docs/account/your-data).
- If you delete your account, you give up your seat. If yours is the last seat on your company's account, your listing stays yours, as described above.

## What a seat can do

On every plan, including Free, you can:

- see everything in the vendor portal, except the **Billing** tab, which only owners see,
- edit your company details, and each product's description, website, logo and categories,
- mark your company details, a product, or a product's integration list as "Looks right", and work through the checklists ([Your checklists](/docs/vendors/checklists)),
- manage seats and your licenses, if you are an owner,
- add a product, and accept or decline a proposed one, if you are an owner ([Adding a product](/docs/vendors/editing-profile-and-products#adding-a-product)),
- claim, edit, retire and add the integrations your company owns, except one delivered through a connector ([Owning an integration](/docs/vendors/owning-an-integration)),
- add your own links to an integration at either end,
- see the reviews of your products, and withdraw your company's reply to one ([Replying to reviews](/docs/vendors/replying-to-reviews)),
- request a change to a detail on an integration your company does not own ([Requesting changes and appeals](/docs/vendors/requesting-changes-and-appeals)),
- maintain the catalog of a connector product your company makes, on that product's **Catalog** tab, once we have handed the catalog to you ([For connector vendors](/docs/vendors/connector-vendors)).

On a product with Managed, you can also:

- edit a product's integrations page URL, API docs URL, trades, audiences, phases and "How teams use it",
- confirm or deny data flows ([Confirming integration data](/docs/vendors/confirming-integration-data)),
- claim, edit, retire and restore an integration your company owns that is delivered through a connector, and decide change requests on it ([Owning an integration](/docs/vendors/owning-an-integration)),
- reply in public to reviews of your products ([Replying to reviews](/docs/vendors/replying-to-reviews)).

Where your company and products appear in search is worked out from how well each listing matches the search and how complete it is. See [How ranking works](/docs/trust/how-ranking-works).

## If a Managed plan ends

A product whose license ends moves to Free. Your seats stay, and so does sign-in. The portal becomes read-only for anything that needs Managed. Nothing you entered is removed. Your listings stay published, and everything Free allows keeps working.
